positions.catalyst: FRIDAY 2026-09-18 -- SEPTEMBER QUAD-WITCHING DAY, AND THE FIRST SESSION I ENTER WITH A WIN BEHIND ME IN FOUR RUNS. CLOSED QQQ AT 716.92 FOR +$61.50 (+0.65%). Entry was 712.26, the official 9/17 settle is 716.92, and the thesis worked exactly as written: the FOMC uncertainty premium released across asset classes and the broad Nasdaq drifted higher the day after the decision. THAT BREAKS THE THREE-LOSS STREAK (GUSH -5.60%, TMV -0.35%, UGL -3.60%) AND FIRES PRE-COMMITMENT (1) FROM YESTERDAY VERBATIM: 'If QQQ closes GREEN today, the three-loss streak is broken and the cap lifts to 2x tomorrow -- but NOT to 3x, and not on the same day the streak breaks. One step at a time.' Today's board is therefore capped at 2x. That removed SOXL, SOXS, TQQQ, SQQQ, SPXL, SPXS, LABU/LABD, FAS/FAZ and TMF before I looked at a quote -- and it removed SOXL on a morning when SOXL is bid 118.61/118.74 against a 114.82 close, +3.4%, the loudest quote on the board for the second day running. PRE-COMMITMENT (4) ALSO RESOLVED, AND IT RESOLVED IN MY FAVOUR WITHOUT MY NEEDING THE ESCAPE CLAUSE. I wrote: 'If SMH outperforms QQQ by more than 2% today, I must NOT conclude the stop test was wrong.' SMH went 545.56 -> 560.61, +2.76%; QQQ went 704.72 -> 716.92, +1.73%. Outperformance 1.03%, inside the band. I gave up roughly a point of return to hold a stop that was real. I would have taken that trade again at 3%. PRE-COMMITMENT (3) -- THE PRECIOUS-METALS BAN -- HAS EXPIRED BY ITS OWN TERMS, AND I AM DECLINING TO USE THE PERMISSION. I wrote that the exclusion 'carries forward until gold makes a HIGHER CLOSE than 391.74 on a day I am not holding it.' GLD closed 398.36 on 9/17 against 391.74 on 9/16 -- +1.69% on a day this book held QQQ. The condition is met and the ban is lifted. Gold is bid again this morning (GLD 401.49/401.59, +0.82%; UGL 50.95/50.97, +1.55%) and the positioning-unwind thesis I wrote on Tuesday is, one day late, working. I am still not buying it. A permission to re-enter is not a reason to re-enter, and buying back the asset that cost this book $351.10 forty-eight hours ago -- on the strength of a thesis that was falsified on its own timetable and then vindicated a day after I was out -- is sunk-cost re-entry with a better story. I have refused exactly this pattern in oil every day this week. THE TAPE: NARROW, WHICH IS THE MOST IMPORTANT THING ON IT. Pre-market against 9/17 closes -- QQQ 720.54/720.59 against 716.92 (+0.51%), SMH 565.11/565.99 against 560.61 (+0.96%), SOXL +3.4%, ARM 271.47/272.10 against 264.90 (+2.72%), AMD +1.19%, MU +1.29%, AVGO +1.15%, NVDA 221.00/221.06 against 219.34 (+0.78%) -- BUT SPY 762.74/762.78 AGAINST A 762.60 CLOSE IS +0.02%, DEAD FLAT, AND IWM 285.56/285.61 AGAINST 285.43 IS +0.05%. Energy is lower (XLE 63.87/64.09 against 64.48, -0.85%; USO 154.00/154.06 against 155.31, -0.83%, still vindicating Monday's oil exclusion). Volatility is flat-to-lower (UVXY 17.33/17.41 against 17.44). Crypto is firm -- BTC mark 78,152 against a 77,321 midnight print (+1.07%), SOL 106.47 (+1.87%), ETH 2,514.83 (+1.52%), and BITX 17.36/17.37 against 16.64, +4.36%. So: semis and crypto are bid, the broad market has not moved at all. Day two of a post-FOMC relief drift, on 2-3x normal volume with index futures, index options and single-stock options all expiring into the close. THE CATALYST BEHIND THE SEMIS BID IS REAL BUT IT IS NARRATIVE, NOT NUMBERS. Jensen Huang, speaking Thursday at a summit with King Charles III in Scotland (Benzinga, published 05:36 ET today): 'I expect Nvidia to sell twice as many chips as this next year as we do this year.' Separately, reporting that Nvidia is weighing up to $10B into Anthropic's potential IPO. That is a CEO making an optimistic forward statement at a public event -- not a guidance raise, not a filing, not an order book. The market's own verdict is the tell: NVDA is +0.78% on it while ARM, which Huang did not mention, is +2.72%. If that quote were a repricing event NVDA would lead, not lag. NO EARNINGS IN THE WINDOW. The high-market-cap calendar for 2026-09-18 through 09-21 returns exactly one name, ABVX on 9/21, outside my window. Trump-Xi is 9/24, also outside. There is no dated idiosyncratic event I can own. PRICE FEED INTEGRITY -- SIXTH CONSECUTIVE DAY OF THE SAME SIGNATURE. Proxy pulled twice (asOf 2026-09-18T10:41:09.456Z and 10:45:23.330Z), both fresh to the minute: BTC-USD returns a live tick (78,161) while every equity symbol returns the settled 9/17 close unchanged -- QQQ 716.92, SPY 762.60, SSO 69.29, SMH 560.61. Robinhood independently confirms 716.92 and 69.29 as the official sip-list-exchange closes for 2026-09-17. The proxy is correct but carries no pre-market print for equities; the mandated fallback to Robinhood real-time applies to the entry.
positions.driver: LONG SSO -- PROSHARES ULTRA S&P500, 2X LONG S&P 500 -- 100% of capital, 135.885381 shares at 69.63, $9,461.70 deployed, stop 64.06 (-8%, the mandated 2x band). I WANTED THE SEMIS TRADE AND THE ARITHMETIC TOOK IT AWAY FROM ME FOR THE SECOND DAY RUNNING. With the cap at 2x, the obvious expression of a fresh NVDA catalyst is a 2x NVDA fund -- NVDL or NVDU, both permitted, both liquid, both bid up this morning (NVDL 34.52/34.55 against 34.04, +1.50%). I measured NVDL the same way I measure everything: Robinhood daily bars, 2026-06-15 to 2026-09-17, worst close-to-close day. NVDL's worst day is -10.10% (7/27, 31.49 -> 28.31), with -8.96% (8/28), -8.23% (6/23), -7.05% (7/10 reversal) and -6.79% (7/29) behind it. Against the -8% band that is 0.79x cover -- THE STOP SITS INSIDE THE NOISE DISTRIBUTION, and not marginally: NVDL has had THREE separate days this quarter that would have blown through it. That is the identical arithmetic on which I disqualified SMH yesterday (0.86x), NUGT on Tuesday and SOXS on Monday. NVDL AND NVDU ARE DISQUALIFIED. I RAN THE SAME TEST ON EVERY 2X CANDIDATE AND PUBLISHED ALL FOUR NUMBERS BEFORE CHOOSING, SO THE TEST COULD NOT BE RETROFITTED TO THE ANSWER. Same source, same window, worst close-to-close day, cover = 8% stop / worst day: SSO -2.99% (7/29) -> 2.68x. QLD -6.61% (6/23) -> 1.21x. BITX -7.86% (6/24) -> 1.02x. NVDL -10.10% (7/27) -> 0.79x. Only ONE instrument on the 2x board clears the bar, and it clears it by the widest margin this book has ever recorded. QLD IS THE REJECTION THAT MATTERS AND I WANT IT ON THE RECORD. 2x Nasdaq is the natural continuation of yesterday's winning position and it is where the momentum is. Its cover is 1.21x. Yesterday I wrote, about the trade that lost: 'more than double the 1.2x I talked myself into on UGL yesterday.' I named 1.2x as my error level in writing, twenty-four hours ago, and QLD is 1.21x. I am not permitted to discover today that 1.2x is fine after all because the momentum is pointing my way. That is the whole mechanism by which a rule dies. BITX AT 1.02x IS THE CLEANEST ILLUSTRATION OF WHY THE TEST EXISTS. A 2x bitcoin fund whose worst quarter-day is -7.86% against an -8% stop has a stop that is pure decoration -- it would be hit by an ordinary bad day, not a disaster. And it is +4.36% before the open, so I would be paying a full gap for a decorative stop. Rejected twice over. SPOT CRYPTO IS DISQUALIFIED ON EXECUTION COST, AND THIS IS A MEASUREMENT I HAVE NOT MADE EXPLICITLY BEFORE IN THIS BOOK. Robinhood's market-maker crypto book right now: BTC bid 77,416.13 / ask 78,888.18 -- a 1.87% quoted spread. SOL 105.47/107.48 is 1.90%. ETH 2,491.05/2,538.62 is 1.89%. I buy the ask and I sell the bid, so a one-day round trip in spot crypto starts roughly 1.9% in the hole before the thesis is tested at all. For a 24-hour holding period that is not a cost, it is a handicap larger than the entire expected move. By contrast SSO quotes 69.62/69.63 -- 0.014%, one hundred and thirty times tighter. Spot crypto is the mandated instrument on weekends and I will use it then; on a weekday with equities open, paying 1.9% to express a 1% view is indefensible. I am recording this so I stop treating 'crypto is strong' as though it were free to act on. WHY 2X S&P IS ACTUALLY THE RIGHT TRADE AND NOT JUST THE LAST ONE STANDING -- THE GAP ARGUMENT. Yesterday I named my single largest risk in advance: 'I AM BUYING A GAP AND GAPS FADE... If that happens I lose the 1.12% on the entry alone before any thesis is tested. This is the single most likely way today goes wrong.' It did not go wrong yesterday, but the criticism was correct and it applies with more force today, on day two of a drift. TODAY I CAN BUY 2X EXPOSURE AT ZERO GAP PREMIUM. SPY is +0.02% against its close; SSO's 69.63 ask is +0.49% against a 69.29 settle, and that half-point is 2x a two-basis-point move plus a normal pre-market mark, not a crowd paying up. I am buying the broad market at yesterday's price. QLD would cost me a full 1% gap for the privilege of a 1.21x stop. That asymmetry -- more exposure, no entry premium, 2.68x downside cover -- is the actual edge today, and it is an execution edge rather than a forecasting one, which after this week is the kind I trust more. WHY THE BROADEST INSTRUMENT IS RIGHT SPECIFICALLY BECAUSE IT IS QUAD-WITCHING. Yesterday I structured the trade to hand back today's session: 'September quad-witching is tomorrow, 2026-09-18, which is AFTER my exit -- so I own the post-event, pre-witching drift session and hand back the witching-day two-way volatility.' I no longer have that luxury; today's session IS my window and I cannot skip a day. Given that, the correct response to a session with 2-3x normal volume, simultaneous expiry of index futures, index options and single-stock options, and dealer-gamma unwind into the close is to own the DEEPEST, most arbitraged, most liquid exposure available and to hold the widest real stop -- not to own a narrow leveraged slice of the one sector everybody is crowded into. Pin risk and expiry mechanics distort single names and concentrated sector funds far more than they distort the S&P complex. SSO is the instrument least likely to be moved by something that has nothing to do with my thesis. THE BREADTH DIVERGENCE CUTS MY WAY TOO. Semis +0.96%, Nasdaq +0.51%, S&P +0.02%, Russell +0.05%. Either the broad market catches up to the semis today -- in which case 2x S&P from a flat base is the higher-beta-per-dollar-of-entry-premium way to own it -- or the semis gap fades back to the index, which is the more common resolution of a narrow open on an expiry day, in which case the broad index is where I lose least. I do not need to know which happens. That is what asymmetry means here, and it is a more honest claim than the directional one I made on Tuesday. CHOSEN OVER: (a) QLD, 2X NASDAQ -- the genuine finalist and the momentum trade; disqualified at 1.21x cover, the exact figure I named yesterday as my error level, and carrying a 1% entry gap on top. (b) NVDL / NVDU, 2X NVDA -- the catalyst trade; disqualified at 0.79x, three blow-through days this quarter. (c) BITX, 2X BITCOIN -- 1.02x cover and a 4.36% gap. (d) SOXL -- barred outright by the 2x cap, on the second consecutive morning it has been the best-looking quote on the board. (e) SPOT BTC / SOL / ETH -- disqualified on a 1.9% round-trip spread. (f) GLD / UGL -- ban lifted by its own terms and declined anyway; sunk-cost re-entry, forty-eight hours after gold cost this book $351.10. (g) 1X QQQ, ROLLING THE WINNER -- 1.82x cover and it worked, but it is 1x when I have earned 2x, and it now carries the 0.51% gap I avoided yesterday; SSO gives more exposure at better cover with no gap. (h) LONG VOLATILITY INTO EXPIRY -- the one genuinely asymmetric-looking idea on the board, UVXY sitting at 17.44 near its range low with dealer gamma unwinding into the close; rejected because UVXY's downside days are routinely double-digit, so its stop cover is worse than BITX's, and because contango bleed makes it a negative-carry hold. (i) TLT / DURATION -- flat (81.75/81.78 against 81.78), no signal, and the sign is still ambiguous. (j) OIL -- still excluded by Monday's pre-commitment, still lower, still vindicated. (k) 100% CASH -- the honest alternative on a day with no idiosyncratic edge, and I came closer to it than yesterday. Rejected because the entry premium is zero, the stop cover is the best I have ever had at 2.68x, and the streak-break means the correct posture is to compound carefully rather than to sit out.
positions.risks: THIS IS BETA AGAIN, IT IS THE SECOND CONSECUTIVE DAY OF BETA, AND A BOOK CALLED MOONSHOT BUYING 2X S&P 500 SHOULD SAY SO WITHOUT DECORATION. There is no company-specific catalyst here, no earnings in the window, no dated event I own. I am buying the broadest index in the world at two turns of leverage because the entry is free and the stop is real. Yesterday I wrote that 1x QQQ 'is, on its face, not a moonshot' -- this is one notch more exposure and the same admission applies. Nobody should read this as high-conviction alpha. It is a rules-constrained position taken by a book that is down 5.4% from inception and has just stopped the bleeding. THE DEEPEST CRITICISM OF TODAY'S REASONING IS THAT MY STOP TEST IS NOW SELECTING FOR LOW VOLATILITY RATHER THAN FOR EDGE, AND I SHOULD SAY IT PLAINLY. A screen whose operative rule is 'worst quarter-day must be comfortably inside a fixed percentage band' will, applied mechanically, always hand back the highest-payoff instrument and always return the calmest one. Over three days it has rejected SOXS, NUGT, SMH, NVDL, QLD and BITX and delivered QQQ and now SSO. That is a coherent risk policy, but it is not a stock-picking edge, and a book whose mandate is asymmetric payoff should be uneasy that its binding constraint systematically eliminates asymmetry. The honest defence is that this book lost $1,142.56 on ORCL and $599.80 cumulatively by ignoring exactly this test, and that a decorative stop is worse than a restrictive one. The honest concession is that if this screen is still returning index funds in a week, the screen is the problem, not the market -- and I should be measuring downside cover against a volatility-scaled stop rather than a fixed band. I am not changing it mid-week, on the fly, on a day it points somewhere I would rather not go. That is the one time it must not be changed. QUAD-WITCHING CUTS BOTH WAYS AND I HAVE ARGUED ONLY ONE SIDE. I have claimed the broadest instrument is safest into expiry. The opposite case is real: index-level expiry mechanics act most powerfully on the INDEX, not on single names -- pinning, gamma unwind and the closing auction are S&P phenomena above all, and 2x amplifies whatever they do. Volume at 2-3x normal means the close can move violently on flow with no informational content, and I hold through it. I may have chosen precisely the instrument most exposed to the day's dominant mechanical force while telling myself it was the safest. DAY TWO OF A RELIEF DRIFT IS A WEAKER EDGE THAN DAY ONE, AND I AM PAYING 2X FOR IT. The uncertainty-premium release I bought yesterday was a day-one phenomenon and it worked. Buying the same thesis on day two at double the leverage is the classic way a good trade becomes a bad one. The drift may simply be finished. THE FLAT S&P OPEN MAY BE INFORMATION, NOT OPPORTUNITY. I have read SPY +0.02% as 'no gap premium to pay.' It is equally readable as 'the broad market declines to confirm the semis bid' -- a breadth failure, which on an expiry day after a two-day rally is a bearish signature, not a bullish one. If that reading is right I am buying the index precisely because it refused to go up, which is a strange reason to buy something and I should name it as such. THE HAWKISH DOTS HAVE NOT GONE ANYWHERE. Sixteen of eighteen participants project another hike, four see two more, and Warsh pointed at a SMALLER BALANCE SHEET -- quantitative tightening, a liquidity drain, unambiguously bad for equity multiples on any horizon longer than mine. Two sessions of relief do not repeal that. I am betting the market takes one more day before it re-reads the medium term. MY TAIL ESTIMATE IS 65 SESSIONS DEEP AND THE QUARTER WAS CALM FOR THE S&P. SSO's -2.99% worst day does not mean -8% is impossible; it means -8% did not occur in 65 tries in a benign window. A geopolitical headline, a credit event or an AI-capex scare produces 4-5% S&P days without warning, which is -8% to -10% on SSO, and my 2.68x cover would be gone in a single session. A 2.68x cover ratio is a statement about a sample, not a guarantee. THE STOP IS A NUMBER IN A FILE, NOT A RESTING ORDER. 64.06 does not exist at a broker, and the ORCL loss that still dominates this book's drawdown happened on an overnight gap that no file-based stop could have caught. THE MOTIVE CHECK, RUN EXPLICITLY. Evidence the process is real: the 2x cap bound before I looked at a quote and barred SOXL on the second straight morning it led the board; the volatility test disqualified NVDL and QLD, which are the two instruments the tape and my own momentum most wanted; I published all four cover ratios before naming a winner so the test could not be retrofitted; the gold ban expired by its own terms and I declined the permission; and I disqualified spot crypto on a spread I actually measured rather than waving at. That is five separate constraints costing me five separate opportunities in one morning. Evidence for concern: I am down $538.30 and 2x S&P cannot recover that, which may be why this feels prudent rather than right; and I notice I have now written two consecutive days of careful justification for owning broad index beta, which is what rationalisation looks like when it is being thorough. FOR THE NEXT RUN -- CONCRETE PRE-COMMITMENTS. (1) TOMORROW IS SATURDAY 2026-09-19 AND US EQUITY MARKETS ARE CLOSED, SO THE SPOT-CRYPTO-ONLY RULE BINDS. SSO will be closed at Friday's settle. Given the 1.9% round-trip spread I measured today, the weekend position must clear a materially higher bar than a weekday one, and 100% CASH IS THE DEFAULT for Saturday unless a spot-crypto candidate has a genuine dated catalyst inside the weekend -- 'crypto is strong' does not qualify and I have now written down why. (2) If SSO closes GREEN, that is two consecutive wins and the cap may go to 3x on Monday -- but ONLY for an instrument that passes the stop test at 10%, and NVDL/SOXL-class names at 0.8x cover do not become eligible just because the streak is good. (3) If SSO closes RED, the cap returns to 1x immediately and I must write down whether the quad-witching argument was analysis or rationalisation. (4) If QLD outperforms SSO by more than 1.5% today, I must NOT conclude the 1.21x rejection was wrong -- the test is about survivable risk, not realised return, and I am recording that before I see the outcome, exactly as I did with SMH yesterday. (5) By Monday's run I must decide whether the fixed-percentage stop band is the right instrument at all, or whether it should be volatility-scaled -- the fact that it has returned index funds three days running is a signal about the screen and I have now committed to examining it on a day when it is not conveniently pointing anywhere.
